newsitem.title: Australia: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - July 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - July 2.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

The South Sydney rugby league club has threatened to sue Optus Vision if the club is excluded from an elite competition after a possible merger with Super League. Club president George Piggins says Souths has been given a verbal contract in front of 30 witnesses which should be honoured. Page 22.

Star Essendon Australian Football League player James Hird has ended weeks of speculation over his playing future by signing for a further three years with his club. The deal is believed to be worth more than A$1 million over three years. Page 22.

The Australian Cricket Board has recommended that Test matches against South Africa later this season be played under lights. This would enable play to continue despite poor natural light conditions, and the proposal is expected to be approved by the International Cricket Council's new sub-committee. Page 22.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australia's leading rugby league clubs from both warring competitions will be warned of possible mergers over the next few days after further peace talks between the leagues yesterday. The detailed content of yesterday's talks is confidential at this stage. Page 52.

A number of countries have made offers to play the Australian soccer team after recent successful games. World Cup champions Brazil have offered to come to Australia and play two matches this year, but the series is unlikely for financial reasons. Page 5.

Controversial Western Reds Super League player Mark Geyer was suspended yesterday for three weeks for a tackle in his first game back after a 10-game suspension for eye gouging and a high tackle. Geyer pleaded guilty to a grade two careless high tackle during last weekend's game. Page 51.
THE AGE

Support for Richmond Australian Football League coach Robert Walls has been confirmed after a lengthy board meeting last night. Club president Leon Daphne says Walls has the board's support, but his tenure at the club will be reviewed at the end of the year. Page B16.

Australian motorcycle champion Michael Doohan is seeking an upgrade in his contract with Honda before he will sign a two-year contract. Doohan says he has the motivation to race until the end of the 1999 season, and has received offers from rival teams Yamaha and Suzuki. Page B14.

The Australian cricket team has defeated Hampshire by an innings and 133 runs in a win described as the best performance on tour. Pace bowler Jason Gillespie came back into contention for a Test berth after a standout performance of five wickets for 35 runs. Page B14.
THE HERALD SUN

The Melbourne Cricket Ground, administered by the Melbourne Cricket Club, is facing a battle to remain Australia's leading cricket venue. The Victorian Cricket Association is considering an option to play at the new Docklands stadium, which could lead to Test and international one-day cricket being taken away from the historic ground. Page 88.

Australian tennis player Jason Stoltenberg lost his match to third seed Yevgeny Kafelnikov at Wimbeldon yesterday, hampered by a number of dubious line calls. Australians making it into the fourth-round from the latest matches include Pat Rafter and Todd Woodbridge. Page 83.

New Zealand rugby union coach John Hart believes the Australian team's recent narrow wins over France have given them the advantage leading into this weekend's Bledisloe Cup Test match in Christchurch. New Zealand's recent matches have been high-scoring wins against Argentina. Page 80.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Australian rugby union player David Giffin has broken his foot after team-mate Ewen McKenzie accidentally trod on it at training yesterday. Giffin is likely to be out of the game for a month, with Garrick Morgan being brought into the squad. Page 88.

The Australian Rugby League has announced some surprise selections in a Rest of the World team to play Australia later this month. Willie McLean, who has played only one first grade match, will represent New Zealand, with two other players on the team also boasting less than ten first grade match experiences. Page 82.

The Australian women's softball team leaves the country today for a series of international matches in the United States next week. The team is ranked third in the world and will play against top competition with the aim of improving their ranking. Page 5.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
